source_text: XII. Ταῦτα δὲ καὶ ἕτερα πλείονα λέγων, θάρσους καὶ χαρᾶς ἐνεπίμπλατο, καὶ τὸ πρόσωπον αὐτοῦ χάριτος ἐπληροῦτο, ὥστε οὐ μόνον μὴ συμπεσεῖν ταραχθέντα ὑπὸ τῶν λεγομένων πρὸς αὐτόν, ἀλλὰ τοὐναντίον τὸν ἀνθύπατον ἐκστῆναι, πέμψαι τε τὸν ἑαυτοῦ κήρυκα, ἐν μέσῳ τοῦ σταδίου κηρῦξαι τρὶς Πολύκαρπος ὡμολόγησεν ἑαυτὸν Χριστιανὸν εἶναι. Τούτου λεχθέντος ὑπὸ τοῦ κήρυκος, ἅπαν τὸ πλῆθος ἐθνῶν τε καὶ Ἰουδαίων τῶν τὴν Σμύρναν κατοικούντων ἀκατασχέτῳ θυμῷ καὶ μεγάλῃ φωνῇ ἐπεβόα· Οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ τῆς Ἀσίας διδάσκαλος, ὁ πατὴρ τῶν Χριστιανῶν, ὁ τῶν ἡμετέρων θεῶν καθαιρέτης, ὁ πολλοὺς διδάσκων μὴ θύειν μηδὲ προσκυνεῖν. Ταῦτα λέγοντες ἐπεβόων καὶ ἠρώτων τὸν Ἀσιάρχην Φίλιππον ἵνα ἐπαφῇ τῷ Πολυκάρπῳ λέοντα. Ὁ δὲ ἔφη μὴ εἶναι ἐξὸν αὐτῷ, ἐπειδὴ πεπληρώκει τὰ κυνηγέσια. Τότε ἔδοξεν αὐτοῖς ὁμοθυμαδὸν ἐπιβοῆσαι ὥστε τὸν Πολύκαρπον ζῶντα κατακαῦσαι. Ἔδει γὰρ τὸ τῆς φανερωθείσης ἐπὶ τοῦ προσκεφαλαίου ὀπτασίας πληρωθῆναι, ὅτε ἰδὼν αὐτὸ καιόμενον προσευχόμενος εἶπεν ἐπιστραφεὶς τοῖς σὺν αὐτῷ πιστοῖς προφητικῶς· Δεῖ με ζῶντα καῆναι.
thought_title: The crowd demands Polycarp be burned alive
orientation: After Polycarp refuses the proconsul's threats of beasts and fire, the proconsul has his herald proclaim three times in the stadium that Polycarp has confessed to be a Christian.
pass_a_gloss: Saying these things and still more besides, he was being filled with boldness and joy, and his face was being filled with grace, so that not only did he not collapse, having been troubled by the things said to him, but on the contrary the proconsul was astounded, and sent his own herald to proclaim three times in the middle of the stadium, Polycarp has confessed himself to be a Christian. When this was said by the herald, the whole multitude both of Gentiles and of Jews dwelling in Smyrna with uncontrollable anger and with a great voice kept shouting out: This is the teacher of Asia, the father of the Christians, the destroyer of our gods, the one teaching many not to sacrifice nor to worship. Saying these things they kept shouting and kept asking the provincial official Philip that he loose a lion upon Polycarp. But he said that it was not permitted for him, since he had completed the beast fights. Then it seemed good to them with one accord to shout out that Polycarp be burned living. For it was necessary that the thing of the vision manifested upon the pillow be fulfilled, when, seeing it burning, while praying he said, having turned to the faithful with him, prophetically: I must be burned living.

choices.why: brief glossary requires confess for ὁμολογέω in open declaration before authority

has admitted he is a Christian

pass_b_english: As Polycarp said this and much more, he was filled with boldness and joy, and his face was full of grace. He did not collapse, shaken by what was said to him. On the contrary, the proconsul himself was astounded and sent his own herald to stand in the middle of the stadium and proclaim three times, "Polycarp has confessed himself to be a Christian."

When the herald said this, the whole crowd of pagans and Jews who lived in Smyrna shouted with uncontrollable anger and a loud voice, "This is the teacher of Asia, the father of the Christians, the destroyer of our gods, who teaches many neither to sacrifice nor to worship." As they said this they kept shouting and asking the provincial official Philip to loose a lion on Polycarp. But he said it was not permitted for him, because he had completed the beast fights. Then they agreed with one mind to shout that Polycarp should be burned alive.
For the vision he had seen upon the pillow had to be fulfilled, when he saw it burning as he prayed and turned to the faithful with him and said prophetically, "I must be burned alive."
